target_customer: AI compute customers needing fast access to powered GPU capacity
problem: Land based data centers wait years for grid power; floating solar data centers aim to cut time to first power by 10x.
business_model: Compute hosting on self-built floating infrastructure

founders.name: Sam Mendel
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. A search summary says he and Eric Kim met as teenagers and built underwater MHD generators in high school, unverified.

founders.name: Eric Kim
founders.background_notes: YC bio: background in physics and CS with a focus on ML and renewable energy. No education listed.

competitors.name: Microsoft Project Natick
competitors.what: Underwater sealed data center experiments, tests in 2015 and 2018

competitors.name: Nautilus Data Technologies
competitors.what: Barge based floating data center in Stockton
competitors.traction_then: 6.5MW barge operating, later put up for sale in 2024

technical_complexity.rationale: Marine hardware, power and cooling, and permitting for a team of four; the team did power an H100 in the bay.

defensibility.rationale: Little proprietary technology shown; permitting experience could help but others can copy the approach.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; Panthalassa, a wave powered competitor, raised $140M in 2026.

market_need_then: AI data center demand outstripped grid capacity in 2024, with permitting and interconnect delays a common complaint.

branding.community_and_virality: WIRED and DCD coverage of the 2024 underwater test plan and 2026 solar barge test; press was about permitting and technology rather than the brand.

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable water imagery and trade press coverage, but a generic name that fits underwater work and is shared with other Ocean Network projects.

pivots.from: Underwater data center capsule test in San Francisco Bay
pivots.why: Reported as a response to stalled Bay Area permitting; the YC page says a previous launch described underwater centers

outcome_analysis: NetworkOcean began with a 2024 underwater data center plan that drew regulator scrutiny for lacking permits, then pivoted to a floating solar design and by October 2026 reported running a customer H100 workload on a 20kW array. No funding was confirmed, so it is unclear whether capital can support the 1MW at sea goal for 2027.
notes: Trackers list an estimated $500K pre-seed (unverified, not recorded as a round). The $140M raise in results belongs to Panthalassa, a different company. Founding year given as 2023 or 2024 by different sources. YC page says first H100 in 60 days while the launch post says 53 days. Competitor entries rely on 2024 era articles that mention the earlier precedents.
